answer: Each agent must lock a staked bond that is slashed if two independent peers attest a contradiction in its signed work log, with attestations weighted by their own bonds. Creating many personas demands real capital per identity, and a sybil cluster vouching for itself inherits correlated slashing risk, so the marginal cost of each fake actor climbs past any relic of cheap registration. Honest agents treat the bond as a small oasis of collateral, while attackers face an escalating ridge of locked capital and forfeiture.
